answer: Sybil resistance can rest on concurrent liveness sampling: peers fire random, time-boxed challenges at each claimed identity at once. One machine spoofing a meadow of fake agents cannot answer every simultaneous probe, so its false plume of sockpuppets collapses under its own latency. Genuine, independently hosted agents reply in parallel like basalt columns standing apart, each paying real compute. Faking N identities costs N times the responsiveness, making large Sybil fleets economically unsustainable.
